name: agent-surfaces
responsibility: The agent of a page over its panes, as the shell places it: the root that holds it, the dock, the conversation panel, the voice over a pane, the Talk and Narrate keys, and a recorded talk's voice
description: @archboard/agent-surfaces, one entry (src/ui/api/agent-surfaces.ts) at the layer above workbench, split from workbench's browser half and from the assembly apps/web made of it (ADR 0092, TASK-653.13). Its eleven names: AgentRoot({ activePaneId, openAnswerFile, chooseShownConversation, children }), AgentDock, AgentPanel, AgentPane({ paneId, conversation, recording, dockless, reducedMotion }), TalkControl, NarrateKey (with the Narrate key's hook inside), useAgentVoice, useAgentPanel, RecordedVoice({ level, children }), RecordedVoiceBox({ transcript, presented }) and AgentAnswer, with their types. The shell passes only its own facts; the root composes the owners, the setup, the voice session, the actions, the draft and the panel. The pane session keeps each socket and its conversation; AgentPane registers the current generation's conversation as it mounts and withdraws that same registration when a newer socket replaces it or the pane goes. useAgentVoice and useAgentPanel hand out reading functions, so a reply does not draw the shell again. isSpeakingLevel stays private. From workbench it takes only the type of what a page asks voice to narrate, through ./browser-contract.
